> **Due:** Wednesday, September 23, 2026, at 11:59 PM Central Time.

## Purpose

This homework brings together the first three sessions. You will create a
reproducible report, work with a small collection of patient-level vectors,
inspect R object types, repair deliberately messy values, use indexing, and
record the work with Git.

The goal is not merely to obtain numbers. Your source document should make it
possible for another analyst to see what you did, rerun it, and understand your
conclusions.

- <a href="starter/homework01.Rmd" download>Download the R Markdown starter</a>

Your document must render successfully after restarting R. Do not use loops,
user-written functions, data frames, or tidyverse functions for this assignment.
They are either unnecessary here or will be covered later.

## Study vectors

The starter supplies four parallel vectors from a small, synthetic blood
pressure study:

```r
patient_id <- sprintf("P%02d", 1:12)
arm <- rep(c("control", "treated"), 6)
baseline_sbp_text <- c(
  "142", "138", "not recorded", "151", "133", "145",
  "128", "160", "139", "147", "136", "154"
)
week4_sbp_raw <- c(140, 128, 131, 143, 129, 136, 126, 18, 135, 139, NA, 142)
```

Each position refers to the same patient across all four vectors. The value
`"not recorded"` represents a missing baseline measurement. Patient P08's
week-4 value was entered as `18`; source verification established that it
should be `148`.

## Part 1: Inspect before changing anything — 10 points

1. Use `class()`, `typeof()`, and `length()` to inspect
   `baseline_sbp_text` and `week4_sbp_raw`.
2. Verify that all four vectors have equal lengths.
3. Predict the type of `c(baseline_sbp_text[1], week4_sbp_raw[1])`, then run it.
   Explain why R produces that type.

## Part 2: Preserve and clean the raw values — 15 points

1. Create `baseline_sbp_clean` as a copy of `baseline_sbp_text`.
2. Replace `"not recorded"` in the copy with `NA`.
3. Convert the cleaned copy to a numeric vector named `baseline_sbp`.
4. Demonstrate that `baseline_sbp_text` remains unchanged and verify the type
   of `baseline_sbp`.

## Part 3: Named indexing and a documented correction — 15 points

1. Create `week4_sbp` as a copy of `week4_sbp_raw`.
2. Assign `patient_id` as the names of `week4_sbp`.
3. Use the patient name—not its numeric position—to correct P08 from `18` to
   `148`.
4. Print the corrected P08 value and count the missing week-4 measurements.

In one sentence, explain why preserving `week4_sbp_raw` is preferable to
overwriting it.

## Part 4: Select patients with logical conditions — 15 points

Use logical indexing to report:

1. the IDs of all patients in the treated arm;
2. the IDs of patients with both baseline and week-4 measurements observed.

Do not type the requested patient IDs manually.

## Part 5: Calculate and interpret change — 25 points

1. Calculate `sbp_change = week 4 − baseline` for every patient and give the
   resulting vector patient names.
2. Calculate the mean observed change among all patients.
3. Calculate the mean observed change among treated patients.
4. Write three sentences interpreting the results. State the number of
   patients contributing to each mean and explain how missing values were
   handled. Do not make a causal or clinical-effectiveness claim from this
   small synthetic dataset.

## Part 6: Reproducibility and Git — 20 points

1. Before editing, follow the Session 2 course-update procedure and confirm that
   the RStudio Git pane is clean.
2. End the report with `sessionInfo()`.
3. Restart R and render the complete document again.
4. Before each commit, inspect the diff and stage only the files intended for
   that checkpoint.
5. Make at least three meaningful commits as the work develops. Suggested
   checkpoints are:
   - create the homework document;
   - complete inspection and cleaning; and
   - complete analysis and interpretation.
6. Push the final source and rendered HTML files to your private course
   repository. Confirm that both files appear on GitHub and match the files you
   will attach to the submission email.
7. Provide the browser address of your homework folder, using this form:

   ```text
   https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/BIOS6301-mywork/tree/main/work/homework01
   ```

   Confirm that you sent collaborator invitations to the instructor and TA as
   taught in Session 2. Do not make the repository public.

Commit messages should describe completed work. Messages such as `changes` or
`homework` do not provide useful history.
